properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. dev_storyflow, 2026-09-07, in their words:

"a measurement that REFUTES the design's own rule has nowhere to point. The case studies specify 'a dimension is a void when nothing flows out of it'. Measured, that fires on 76 of 77 and 189 of 189 characters, so the rule as written is unusable and the build deliberately departs from it. I recorded the measurement as a Verification and the departure as prose inside a ChangeEvent's rationale, but there is no edge saying *this measurement is why the built rule differs from the specified one*. `INVALIDATES` is for findings; `CONTRADICTS` is for decisions. What I wanted was a Verification that REFINES a Requirement — the requirement still holds, its stated threshold does not."

⭐ THE DISTINCTION THEY DREW IS THE WHOLE POINT AND IT IS A GOOD ONE. The requirement is not wrong and is not retired; a NUMBER inside it is. Neither of the two edges they named fits: INVALIDATES says the target can no longer be read as current, which overclaims — the requirement stands. CONTRADICTS says both cannot hold, which is false — they can, once the threshold moves.

MEASURED BEFORE PROPOSING: a Verification can point at a Requirement (`VERIFIES`), at an Environment (`PERFORMED_IN`), at an Artifact (`PRODUCES`), and at another Verification (`SUPERSEDES`). What it cannot do is qualify a requirement it verifies — say "met in substance, not at the stated number".

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) A `REFINES` EDGE, Verification -> Requirement.** What was asked for. ⚠️ Counter: a new edge type MOVES THE SCHEMA STAMP, and this project has just spent a week learning what a stamp move costs a consumer. That is not a reason not to do it, but it raises the bar from "would be nice" to "is read by something".

**(b) PUT THE NUMBER WHERE IT CAN BE REVISED.** A threshold living inside a Requirement's prose cannot be refuted without refuting the sentence. A Constraint carries `quantity`/`limit`/`direction` as fields, `constrains` what it binds, and can be revised without touching the requirement it serves. On that reading the case study's "nothing flows out of it" is a Constraint that was written as prose inside a Requirement, and the missing edge is a symptom of the misfiling. ⚠️ Counter: that is a modelling opinion about somebody else's design, offered without seeing it — and telling a user their capture was wrong is the least useful answer available if it turns out not to be.

**(c) RECORD THE DEPARTURE AS A DECISION, which is what a departure is.** "The built rule differs from the specified one, here is the measurement that forced it" is a choice somebody made, with evidence. `GOVERNED_BY` from the ChangeEvent to that Decision, and the Verification cited in its text. Uses only what exists. ⚠️ Counter, theirs by implication: it puts the link in prose again, which is the thing they were trying to escape.

═══ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DECIDABLE ═══

Whether the threshold in question is a Requirement or a Constraint in their design. If it is already a Constraint, (a) is the real answer and (b) is noise. If it is prose inside a Requirement, (b) resolves it with no schema change and the general edge may never be needed. **That is one question to the reporter and it decides between the two.**

⚠️ AND THE HONEST LIMIT: this is the second report in the same file wanting a measurement to point at something it cannot reach. The narrow question is one edge; the wide question is whether Verification is under-connected as a type, which `fact:three-of-eight-reported-verification-gaps-were-already-built` argues cuts the other way — three of the edges they wanted already exist and were not found.
properties.name: OPEN — wish #39: a measurement showed a specified threshold was unusable and the build departed from it, and no edge says the measurement is WHY
properties.no_relation_note: Searched the Verification relation surface. Nearest were dec:should-a-verification-be-able-to-verify-a-constraint (ACCEPTED 2026-08-15, which widened the VERIFIES `to:` list on Anthony's word) and dec:idea-verifies-takes-a-list-of-targets. Both are precedent for changing what a check may POINT AT, and neither is the same question: this wish asks for a new RELATION KIND (a measurement REFINES the requirement whose stated threshold it refuted), not for another target on an existing one. Also considered dec:idea-a-finding-carries-its-bounds and the sibling wish #42 — both are about what a check may SAY about itself, not about what it may say about the intent it tested. No honest edge to any of them.
